# Lavendar Lewis

## Overview

- **Age:** 45  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive  <sub>[v4 c3 P30](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0030)</sub>
- **Origin:** East Grafton  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- **Titles:** Miss  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Mother Lavendar  <sub>[v3 c23 P4](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0004)</sub>

## Appearance

She is a petite lady with thick, wavy snow-white hair arranged in puffs and coils, and an almost girlish face with pink cheeks, dimples, sweet lips, and big soft brown eyes. She wears frills, laces, and dainty gowns such as cream muslin patterned with pale roses. Over the years, she changes very little and keeps her youthful look, seeming to have drunk from the Fountain of Youth.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045), [v2 c27 P22](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0022), [v3 c23 P3](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0003), [v4 c3 P30](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0030), [v4 c3 P32](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0032)_

## Personality

Imaginative and youthful at heart, she enjoys "pretending" things and hosting whimsical pretend tea parties regardless of her age. She admits to being a proud and sulky person when offended, which historically led her to prolong quarrels. Despite a past broken heart, she maintains a happy, contented, and resilient disposition, enjoying life's simple pleasures like sweets and dreaming. She is warm, hospitable, and deeply affectionate toward her loved ones and kindred spirits.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P54](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0054), [v2 c21 P57](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0057), [v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003), [v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019)_

## Goals

- To stay true to her lifelong love for Stephen Irving rather than marrying anyone else  <sub>[v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019)</sub>

## History

Lavendar Lewis grew up in East Grafton, where her father named her after the lavender scent he associated with her mother. In her youth, she was engaged to Stephen Irving, but the engagement ended after a foolish quarrel fueled by mutual pride and her own sulkiness. After Stephen left for the United States, she spent decades living a quiet, romantic life at Echo Lodge, taking in a succession of young Bowman handmaidens whom she collectively nicknamed Charlotta. When Anne Shirley and Diana Barry visited Echo Lodge, Miss Lavendar formed a deep friendship with Anne, recognizing her as a kindred spirit. Through Anne's introduction, she met Stephen's son, Paul Irving, which inadvertently led to Stephen learning she remained unmarried and returning to seek her forgiveness. The two reconciled and were married in a ceremony in her honeysuckle arbor before moving to Boston. She later returned to Prince Edward Island for visits, maintaining a loving stepmother relationship with Paul and an enduring closeness with Anne.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086), [v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003), [v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019), [v2 c27 P22](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0022), [v2 c29 P5](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0005), [v2 c30 P29](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0029), [v2 c30 P30](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0030), [v3 c7 P48](../source/v03-c07.md#nw-v03-c07-p0048), [v3 c23 P4](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0004), [v4 c3 P30](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0030)_

## Background by volume

- Named Lavendar by her father because he was fond of the scent  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- Her mother died ten years prior to Anne's visit  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- Engaged twenty-five years ago to Stephen Irving, but broke it off after a petty quarrel driven by pride and sulkiness  <sub>[v2 c22 P9](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0009), [v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019)</sub>
- Hired a series of handmaidens from the Bowman family, calling each one 'Charlotta'  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- Lived a quiet, sequestered life at Echo Lodge in Grafton  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003)</sub>

## Quotes

> But what is the use of being an independent old maid if you can’t be silly when you want to, and when it doesn’t hurt anybody?  <sub>[v2 c21 P57](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0057)</sub>

> Father named me Lavendar because he was so fond of it.  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>

> I knew I would rather be an old maid for a thousand years than marry anybody who wasn’t Stephen Irving.  <sub>[v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019)</sub>

> I’m really a very happy, contented little person in spite of my broken heart.  <sub>[v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019)</sub>

> Oh, sometimes, I think it is of no use to make friends. They only go out of your life after awhile and leave a hurt that is worse than the emptiness before they came.  <sub>[v2 c27 P32](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0032)</sub>
